transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Nora Li (Redwood CSM); Markus Hale (Head of AI, Pacific Arc), Rina Soto (Security Architect), Tommy Ng (Platform Eng), Eva Moreno (Compliance)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Customer evaluating hosting model decision across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, Private for regulated financial workloads.
- Key constraints: EU/US data residency per customer segment, HIPAA for a small pilot product, 7 year retention for audit logs in some jurisdictions, access control and KMS residency.
- Next steps: Redwood to provide security pack and Dedicated sizing; schedule POC.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I think we got most of the calendar folks here. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE.
[00:06] Markus Hale: Hey Alex, hi team, Markus here. We're hoping to walk through the residency decision matrix today. We have some folks from compliance and platform so we can be specific.
[00:12] Alex Kim: Perfect. I'll do a quick framing then Priya will jump into the technical tradeoffs and Nora will handle operational questions.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Hi all, Priya, Redwood SE. I'll try to keep the deep bits straight, but ask me to slow down if I go too fast.
[00:24] Rina Soto: Hi, Rina, security. We have a list of reg questions but mostly about logs, key locations, and residency constraints.
[00:28] Tommy Ng: Tommy, platform. We'll want to see what changes are needed for our deployment pipelines and infra.
[00:33] Eva Moreno: Eva, compliance — quick clarifying Q: when you say "hosted" what's actually stored outside our control? logs? prompt text?
[00:38] Alex Kim: Good question. For Redwood Hosted the control plane and inference runtime are managed by Redwood across our regions. Customer data can be controlled through model pinning and optional request-level encryption but by default request payloads and logs flow into our managed systems — with options for minimization and redaction.
[00:51] Markus Hale: Right, so our product teams want the lowest latency and cost but legal is strict about EU customer data not leaving EU data centers. Also one cohort might be HIPAA-bound.
[01:02] Priya Desai: Ok, so there are three primary hosting options we usually discuss: Hosted (fully managed multi-region), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in a region or set of regions with tenant isolation), and Private (VPC/on-prem with customer-managed control plane). Each has different tradeoffs for latency, operational burden, and evidence you can produce.
[01:20] Markus Hale: Can you quickly map which model lets us keep logs and keys in-region?
[01:25] Priya Desai: Hosted: we provide region selection for runtime and data residency where supported, but some control plane artifacts and global telemetry might still be in Redwood control plane — we can discuss region-locking for enterprise contracts. Dedicated: runtime and logs can be isolated to the region and you can request stricter retention policies. Private: full control, you run the control plane inside your VPC, you manage KMS/HSM; best for strict residency.
[01:42] Rina Soto: You mentioned KMS; does Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS or is it Redwood-managed? We need the keys to be resident in EU for EU data.
[01:48] Priya Desai: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted there are two options: Redwood-managed keys (default) or BYOK for enterprise customers — with BYOK you can keep keys in your cloud KMS in the region. Worth noting: BYOK in Hosted sometimes requires additional compliance agreement.
[02:03] Tommy Ng: How about log retention and the ability to redact PII from logs? Our legal team says we need log retention for audit but also need redaction for PII.
[02:12] Nora Li: We have configurable log pipelines. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention windows and log sinks to your augmentation — e.g., push to your S3 buckets or SIEM and apply redaction there. For Hosted we provide a redaction pass and you can opt-out of storing full request bodies, but we need to discuss tradeoffs: removing request bodies could complicate debugging and model quality audits.
[02:33] Eva Moreno: What's the default log retention on Hosted?
[02:36] Alex Kim: Default is 90 days for request/response traces and 365 days for audit-level events, but enterprise customers often negotiate longer or shorter windows.
[02:45] Markus Hale: For our audit obligations some markets require 7 years of evidence. Does Dedicated give us the ability to store logs for 7 years without Redwood deleting?
[02:54] Priya Desai: Yes, Dedicated and Private allow you to control long-term archives — you can export logs to your storage with lifecycle policies keeping them indefinitely. Hosted can be extended but often requires archiving to customer-owned buckets.
[03:06] Rina Soto: And what about access control — RBAC? We need separation between operations and product teams, and strict audit trails.
[03:13] Priya Desai: We support RBAC with SSO integrations (SAML/SCIM), and audit logs that show token-level access. Dedicated/Private provide stronger isolation for admin roles because you can map to your identity provider and restrict control-plane access to your VPC.
[03:27] Tommy Ng: Any differences in the inference behavior — e.g., KV cache, batching, and model variants — between Hosted and Dedicated? We have performance SLOs.
[03:35] Priya Desai: The runtime is the same code path but kernels and resource allocation differ. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable throughput, and you can pin model versions. Hosted may route to compatible variants for cost/latency tradeoffs. There can be small differences in cold-starts and batching behavior if you use burst policies. We'll document expected p99 latencies given your traffic profile.
[03:58] Markus Hale: We will likely do an initial pilot for a HIPAA use case in the US, then expand to EU customers with residency. For the HIPAA pilot, is Hosted acceptable?
[04:08] Alex Kim: Hosted can be HIPAA-compatible with BAAs and with proper configuration (region selection, encryption, log controls). Many customers run HIPAA workloads on Hosted, but some prefer Dedicated for stronger isolation.
[04:20] Eva Moreno: Our internal counsel will push for Dedicated or Private if they feel the control plane artifacts are out of our control.
[04:26] Rina Soto: Also wanted to bring up the question of cross-border backups and snapshots. If a model snapshot is captured for rollback, where is it stored?
[04:33] Priya Desai: Snapshots for Dedicated are stored in customer-isolated storage in-region if requested. For Hosted, snapshots may be replicated for HA across regions unless you explicitly opt for region-locking on the plan.
[04:45] Markus Hale: Are there any known audit artifacts we can get to show evidence of where data lived and which keys were used?
[04:51] Nora Li: Yes, we provide detailed audit trails: token-level logs, KMS usage logs, control plane event history. For Dedicated/Private, you can push those logs to your SIEM; for Hosted we can provide exports and certificates of residency per request window.
[05:06] Alex Kim: Quick call-out: if it's helpful, we have a one-page residency decision playbook that maps typical regulatory profiles to recommended hosting choices. I'll attach that after the call.
[05:14] Markus Hale: Perfect, that's useful.
[05:17] Tommy Ng: A couple of specific tech deep Qs: 1) If we use BYOK in Hosted, is the decrypted data ever in Redwood-managed memory? 2) Can we enforce that KV cache never persists outside the GPU?
[05:27] Priya Desai: For BYOK the keys live in your KMS; Redwood requests encrypted blobs and decrypts in-memory within the runtime for serving — keys are not stored by Redwood. If you require that decryption only happens inside your VPC, that's Private. Regarding KV cache — the runtime keeps KV caches in memory/GPU and we can configure policies to avoid writing them to disk; for Dedicated/Private we can guarantee that KV won't leave the node. Hosted best-effort but we can't promise zero replication without contract.
[05:52] Rina Soto: So for EU PII we will likely require Private or Dedicated with BYOK. We prefer not to have decrypted PII pass through any global control plane.
[06:01] Priya Desai: Understood. Many of our EU financial customers choose Dedicated with BYOK to balance operational overhead vs full on-prem.
[06:07] Markus Hale: How about incident response — if someone subpoenas logs, how quickly can we produce an audit trail?
[06:13] Nora Li: We can produce audit logs and sign them with tamper-evident checksums. The SLA for evidence production is part of the enterprise contract; typical turnaround is 72 hours for simple exports, faster for urgent items with an escalation path.
[06:26] Eva Moreno: Is there an added cost or complexity for the tamper-evidence?
[06:30] Alex Kim: It's usually part of the enterprise pack; we can include tamper-evidence and longer retention for an add-on.
[06:34] Markus Hale: Pricing? Ballpark for Dedicated for our initial three-model footprint — say average 4 qps with peaks to 12 qps, 8B token/month — can you give rough delta vs hosted?
[06:45] Priya Desai: I can do a back-of-envelope now but will follow up with a detailed sizing doc. Roughly, Dedicated for that profile might be 1.5–2x the hosted per-token unit cost depending on reserved commit and burst capacity. There are also fixed monthly platform fees for Dedicated. I'll put numbers in the pricing sheet.
[07:05] Tommy Ng: For the POC, can we run dedicated-in-region for 2 weeks to verify p99 latency and log export?
[07:10] Priya Desai: Yes, we usually run a short Dedicated proof-of-concept. For that we provision a small GPU pool in your target region, run benchmark scripts, and validate log export and KMS flows. We'll want sample payloads and traffic replay.
[07:22] Markus Hale: We'll need to know what infra changes on our side — like firewalls, VPC peering, egress rules — to enable the Dedicated POC.
[07:30] Alex Kim: We'll provide a VPC runbook and list of required CIDR ranges and ports. For Private you'll need a bit more infra to host the control plane, but for Dedicated it's usually a peering/VPN setup and IAM role trust for storage export.
[07:43] Rina Soto: One more Q on logs: can we redact PII at ingestion time? We have internal tokenizers that mark PII; can we run them before logs leave our environment?
[07:52] Priya Desai: Yes: for Dedicated/Private we can place a logging forwarder in your VPC that performs redaction before sending to Redwood. For Hosted we can set up a pre-processing hook or use customer-side edge redaction, but it's more work.
[08:05] Eva Moreno: Do you have customers in the EU who run similar setups? Any references?
[08:09] Alex Kim: We have a couple of references in EU banking. I'll check which ones are public-ref friendly and share.
[08:14] Markus Hale: Are there any gotchas around cross-service replication — e.g., if we use your embeddings service and another provider in parallel, are we duplicating logs across regions?
[08:23] Priya Desai: That can happen. We recommend centralizing exports to your S3/SIEM in region and controlling cross-region replication there. We'll help map the flow.
[08:33] Tommy Ng: Operational question: what's the upgrade/rollout process for model versions in Dedicated? We cannot have silent quality regressions.
[08:39] Priya Desai: We support pinned model versions and rollout policies (canary, A/B). In Dedicated you control rollout schedules and can set automated fallback to a pinned baseline. Also Redwood Optimize will flag quality regressions against your prompt sets.
[08:53] Markus Hale: Ok that's good.
[08:55] Alex Kim: Maybe let's go through a quick recap and concrete next steps.
[09:00] Nora Li: Recap: Customer needs EU residency for EU customers, HIPAA-compatible pilot in US, long-term audit retention for specific markets, BYOK in region for keys, redaction pipeline for PII, and predictable p99 latency. Redwood suggests Dedicated with BYOK for initial rollout, Private if counsel requires full control.
[09:16] Markus Hale: That sounds right. Can you send the residency playbook and the Dedicated sizing by end of week?
[09:22] Alex Kim: Yes — Alex will share security pack + residency playbook; Priya will share sizing and cost delta; Nora will share runbook for VPC/peering; Tommy will share payloads.
[09:31] Eva Moreno: One last note — our legal wants to understand model output drift and data used for model improvement. If Redwood stores prompts for supervised learning, we need explicit opt-in.
[09:40] Priya Desai: We do not use customer prompts for model training without explicit opt-in. We'll include that in the security pack.
[09:46] Markus Hale: Thanks all, let's reconvene after we review the docs.
[09:50] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone — we'll share follow-ups in the next 48–72 hours.
[09:55] (call ends)
